- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — cap forecast overshoot at +10% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.
- If sentiment is volatile or oscillating, smooth forecast transitions — avoid sharp directional shifts in 3–5 day windows.
- Correct for lag: if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% in 3–5 days, adjust next forecast down by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, assume mean reversion toward 30-day historical average — apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or weak.
